extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care providers, potential sponsors, legal service providers, advocates, and stakeholders commenting on the proposed ORR rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory requirements for placement, services, notice of rights, sponsor suitability, home studies, release approvals, denials, and appeals for unaccompanied children held in ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of unaccompanied children with their children
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes to place unaccompanied children and their children together at the same care provider facilities, except in unusual or emergency situations (proposed §410.1108(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy is not limited to biological children because parentage may be unknown at intake; broader language allows flexibility to account for caretakers who are not biological parents. ORR believes placement together is in the best interests of the children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to colocating parent and child (unusual or emergency situations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual or emergency situations would include, but not be limited to: hospitalization or need for a specialized care or treatment setting that cannot provide appropriate care for the child; a request by the unaccompanied child for alternate placement of the child; and when the unaccompanied child is the subject of substantiated allegations of abuse or neglect against the child (or temporary separation in urgent cases with sufficient evidence) (proposed §410.1108(a)(1)-(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These circumstances codify existing policy and reflect ORR's responsibility to consider the best interests of children when making placement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best-interest consideration when other parent is a U.S. citizen
rubrics_metrics.description: If the child has another parent who is a U.S. citizen present in the U.S., ORR would consider whether it is in the best interests of the child to place the child with the unaccompanied child parent or the U.S. citizen parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR requests comments on this interpretation of its authorities under the TVPRA and the HSA because neither statute expressly contemplates scenarios where an unaccompanied child is a parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services to children of unaccompanied children
rubrics_metrics.description: Children of unaccompanied children would receive the same care and services as ORR provides to the unaccompanied children, as appropriate, regardless of the children's immigration or citizenship status (proposed §410.1108(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: U.S. citizen children of unaccompanied children would be eligible for mainstream public benefits (e.g., Medicaid). Care provider facilities shall submit applications for public benefits on behalf of U.S. citizen children and should exhaust public benefits to the greatest extent practicable before using ORR-funded services (proposed §410.1108(b)(2)). Helping to file for birth certificates or other documentation is included as possible assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide prompt notice of legal rights and Legal Resource Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would be required to promptly provide each unaccompanied child with the information described in §410.1109(a)(1)-(3) in a language and manner the child understands, including a state-by-state list of free legal service providers compiled and annually updated by ORR as part of a Legal Resource Guide (proposed §410.1109(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement aligns with TVPRA and HSA obligations to ensure counsel and guardian/attorney representation services; the list may be compiled/updated by an ORR contractor or grantee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of right of potential review (placement review notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would be required to provide an explanation stating that ORR usually houses persons under 18 in the least restrictive setting and that if the child believes they have not been properly placed or treated, they may call a lawyer and, if unable to afford one, call from the list of free legal services provided with the form (proposed §410.1109(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This updates FSA Exhibit 6 language to reflect current placement requirements and replaces outdated references (e.g., INS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of legal rights and effective communication obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes that a presentation regarding legal rights be provided to each unaccompanied child (proposed §410.1109(a)(3)) and that ORR take appropriate steps to ensure information is communicated effectively to individuals with disabilities and limited English proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes provision of auxiliary aids and services per section 504 and 45 CFR 85.51, and provision of interpreters or translated documents. ORR requests comment on steps to ensure effective communication and meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-retaliation against legal service providers
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall not engage in retaliatory actions against legal service providers or any other practitioner because of advocacy or appearance in an action adverse to ORR (proposed §410.1109(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses ORR's intent to promote and protect unaccompanied children's access to legal counsel notwithstanding general presumptions about government integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and purpose of ‘release’ to a vetted sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Release is defined as the ORR-approved transfer of an unaccompanied child from ORR care and custody to a vetted and approved sponsor in the United States; the released child is no longer in ORR custody (Subpart C, §410.1200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release does not include discharge for reasons such as turning 18, attaining legal immigration status, or removal to home country. Under the FSA, a sponsor assumes custody once a child is released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of preference for release to sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would codify the following order of preference for release: (1) to a parent; (2) to a legal guardian; (3) to an adult relative; (4) to an adult individual or entity designated by the parent or guardian with applicable documentation; (5) to a standard program willing to accept legal custody; (6) to an adult individual or entity seeking custody at ORR's discretion when no family alternative exists (proposed §410.1201(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR views placement with vetted family members or approved sponsors as generally in the best interests of children. Examples for (6) include foster parents or other adults who have built a relationship with the child while in ORR care.

rubrics_metrics.name: No disqualification based solely on sponsor immigration status
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would not disqualify potential sponsors based solely on their immigration status and would not collect or share sponsor immigration status information for law enforcement or immigration enforcement purposes (proposed §410.1201(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on immigration status, if collected, would only be used to evaluate a sponsor's ability to provide care (e.g., plan if undocumented sponsor is detained).

rubrics_metrics.name: No release on child's own recognizance
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall not release unaccompanied children on their own recognizance (proposed §410.1201(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement determinations must follow the statutory and policy frameworks for sponsor vetting and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor application package and language accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential sponsors must complete an application package to be considered, and application packages must be available in the potential sponsor's native or preferred language (proposed §410.1202(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application packages may be obtained from the care provider facility or ORR directly to ensure access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum elements of sponsor suitability assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability assessments will be conducted for all sponsors and at minimum include review of the application package, verification of the proposed sponsor's identity and relationship to the child, and may include consultation with issuing agencies and background checks (proposed §410.1202(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are consistent with 8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(3)(A) and ORR's current policies; ORR may conduct fingerprint-based criminal record checks and other checks as part of assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible additional suitability procedures (home visits, interviews, verification)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may interview household members, conduct a home visit or home study, conduct background and criminal records checks (including biometric/fingerprinting), and verify employment, income, or other information (proposed §410.1202(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment/income verification is a permissible consideration but low income or informal employment will not automatically disqualify a sponsor. Any assessment should consider the wishes and concerns of the minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of prior relationship between sponsor and child
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would assess the nature and extent of the sponsor's previous and current relationship with the unaccompanied child and, if applicable, the child's family, and may deny release to unrelated sponsors who have no pre-existing relationship with the child (proposed §410.1202(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should be read consistently with §410.1201(a)(4) permitting release to an individual designated by parent/guardian; ORR is not required to release to an individual with no prior relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider sponsor motivation and opportunities to build relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would consider the sponsor's motivation for sponsorship; the opportunity for sponsor and child to build a healthy relationship while the child is in ORR care; the child's preferences and the child's parent's or guardian's preferences (proposed §410.1202(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors inform whether proposed sponsorship is likely to support the child's well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of child's individualized risks and concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments should evaluate risks or individual concerns including: (1) victim of sex or labor trafficking or at risk for trafficking; (2) history with criminal or juvenile justice systems; (3) history of behavioral issues; (4) history of violence; (5) individualized needs (disabilities, medical or behavioral/mental health issues); (6) history of substance use; (7) child is a parent or is pregnant (proposed §410.1202(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These risks must be evaluated in conjunction with the child's current functioning and strengths to determine safe placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered regarding sponsor's ability to ensure child well-being
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would consider the potential sponsor's strengths and resources in conjunction with risks such as: (1) criminal background; (2) current illegal drug use or history of abuse/neglect; (3) physical environment of the home; (4) other child welfare concerns (proposed §410.1202(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'other child welfare concerns' is intentionally broad. ORR shall not discriminate against qualified individuals with disabilities. Listed risks are not necessarily disqualifying, but ORR must assess extent and adapt a release plan as needed (§410.1202(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor understanding of child's needs and legal responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would assess the potential sponsor's understanding of the child's needs, plan to provide adequate care, supervision, and housing, understanding of responsibilities related to immigration court proceedings, school attendance, U.S. child labor laws, and awareness of/access to community resources (proposed §410.1202(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assessment evaluates practical caregiver capacity and readiness to meet obligations associated with sponsorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of a release plan including post-release services
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would develop a release plan that could enable a safe release through provision of post-release services, if needed (proposed §410.1202(i) and §410.1203(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans would cover providing adequate care, supervision, access to community resources, housing, and education. ORR shall educate sponsors about the child's needs and work with them to develop appropriate plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR's continuous efforts and information sharing during release approval
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR must make and record timely and continuous efforts toward safe and timely release, including intakes, admissions assessments, and ongoing case management to identify sponsors; and if a potential sponsor is identified, ORR would explain requirements and procedures to both the child and the potential sponsor (proposed §410.1203(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These activities are intended to identify sponsors and keep stakeholders informed throughout the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of sponsor application and Sponsor Care Agreement commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor application must include supporting information/documentation regarding identity, relationship to the child, background on sponsor and household members, ability to provide care, and commitment to obligations in the Sponsor Care Agreement (proposed §410.1203(c)). The Sponsor Care Agreement requires commitments to: (1) provide for child's physical and mental well-being; (2) ensure compliance with DHS and immigration court requirements; (3) adhere to child labor and truancy laws; (4) notify DHS/EOIR and other parties of address changes; (5) provide notice of initiation of dependency proceedings or any risk to the child; (6) for non-parent sponsors, notify ORR of child moving or change of address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In emergencies (e.g., serious illness or destruction of sponsor's home), a sponsor may transfer temporary physical custody of the child but must notify ORR as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after the transfer; ORR is not proposing to require permission for such temporary transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denying release during approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would deny release if it has reason to believe the person or agency may harm or neglect the child, or will fail to present the child before DHS or immigration courts when requested, or otherwise is not willing or able to provide for the child's physical or mental well-being (proposed §410.1203(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include unsafe physical environment, inability/willingness to provide care, or risk to the child or community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home study requirement as part of suitability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of sponsor suitability assessment, ORR may require a home study investigating living conditions, standard of care, and interviews; if required, the home study shall take place prior to the child's physical release (proposed §410.1204(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home studies serve to determine whether a potential sponsor can provide for the child's health, safety, and well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring a home study
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes three circumstances where a home study shall be required (proposed §410.1204(b)): (1) conditions identified in TVPRA (severe trafficking victim, special needs child with disability, child who has been victim of physical/sexual abuse indicating significant harm or threatened harm, or child whose proposed sponsor clearly presents risk based on objective evidence); (2) before releasing any child to a non-relative sponsor seeking to sponsor multiple children or who has previously sponsored/seeks additional children; (3) before releasing any child 12 years old or younger to a non-relative sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR believes the latter two categories align with statutory obligations to ensure sponsors can provide for physical and mental well-being and protect children from traffickers/exploiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR discretion to initiate home studies
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR would have discretion to initiate home studies when it determines a home study is likely to provide additional information useful for determining sponsor suitability (proposed §410.1204(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows ORR to require studies beyond the mandatory circumstances when helpful to ensure child safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider obligations regarding home study process and reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Care providers must inform potential sponsors when planning a home study, explain scope and purpose, answer questions, and provide the home study report to the potential sponsor if the release is denied (proposed §410.1204(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subsequent addendums to the report must also be provided to the potential sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-release services when a home study is conducted
rubrics_metrics.description: An unaccompanied child for whom a home study is conducted shall receive post-release services as described at §410.1210 (proposed §410.1204(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is consistent with statutory follow-up service obligations under 8 U.S.C. 1232(c)(3)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for denial of release to a sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsorship would be denied if ORR determines the proposed sponsor is not capable of providing for the child's physical and mental well-being or the placement would result in danger to the child or community (proposed §410.1205(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials follow from suitability assessments and release-process findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for Notification of Denial letters
rubrics_metrics.description: If ORR denies release to a parent or legal guardian, ORR must notify them in writing; the Notification of Denial must include: (1) explanation of reasons; (2) evidence and information supporting the denial; (3) instructions for requesting an appeal; (4) notice that the potential sponsor may submit additional evidence before a hearing or orally during a hearing; (5) notice that the potential sponsor may present witnesses and cross-examine ORR's witnesses (if willing); (6) notice that the potential sponsor may be represented by counsel at no cost to the Federal Government (proposed §410.1205(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the sole reason for denial is concern the child is a danger to themself or the community, ORR must send the child a copy of the Notification of Denial in a language the child understands; the child may appeal such a denial (§410.1205(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to child and counsel when parent/guardian denied
rubrics_metrics.description: If a potential sponsor who is the child's parent or legal guardian is denied, ORR shall inform the unaccompanied child, the child advocate, and the child's attorney of record or EOIR accredited representative (or local legal service provider if none) of that denial (proposed §410.1205(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures key parties are informed and can assist with appeals or post-decision steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to counsel regarding release or denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaccompanied children may have the assistance of counsel, at no cost to the Federal Government, with respect to release or the denial of release to a proposed sponsor (proposed §410.1205(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR recognizes legal representation assistance in release proceedings and denial appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeal procedures for parents and legal guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Parents and legal guardians denied sponsorship may seek an appeal by submitting a written request to the Assistant Secretary of ACF or the Assistant Secretary's neutral and detached designee; appeals may be sought with or without a hearing pursuant to agency guidance, and the Assistant Secretary or designee will acknowledge the request (proposed §410.1206(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may provide language services during the appeals process subject to resource availability. The child may also appeal when the sole reason for denial is concern about danger to self or others (§410.1206(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Child's ability to appeal denial when danger to self/others is sole reason
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sole reason for denial is that the unaccompanied child is a danger to themself or the community, the unaccompanied child may seek an appeal of the denial and may consult with their attorney of record or a legal service provider for assistance (§410.1206(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The child may seek such appeal at any time after denial while still in ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ninety (90)-day review of pending release applications
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR Federal staff supervising case management must review all pending sponsor applications or Family Reunification Packets (FRP) for unaccompanied children who have been in ORR custody for 90 days after submission to identify and resolve reasons a release remains pending and determine steps to accelerate safe release (proposed §410.1207(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon completion of the review, case managers or designated staff must update the potential sponsor and unaccompanied child on case status and explain reasons the release process is incomplete (§410.1207(b)).
